title: Which AI tool better for trading?
author: cryptign
selftext: Hey guys, which ai tool better for trading ideas or analysis. Lets share your ideas experiences please. Ty

comments.author: Remarkable-Duty8067
comments.body:
Use any AI. Hit the border. Expand. You yet dont know what you want and how to get it. Just start.

After a couple of months and lots of discarded code you eventually figure out how to config your AI, structure your projects (critical! Git doc tree with auto hygiene, no in-app documentation, does the job for me). Then start your project. Get a datapool of 20GB+ and backtest. Do the institutional methods, there is no workaround. Look ahead bias, cut of a holdout frame. Slippage, risk % etc. No guesses. Verification.

When you have no clue, develop an AI feedback loop, copy and paste to external AI, repeat. Deepseek allround, gpt code for.. guess what, Elicit for methodical verification. Let them do the work.

Mark again: Be extremly pedantic with you documentation.

comments.author: Technical_Dish_1898
comments.body:
Wrong axis, honestly — the split that matters isn't GPT vs Claude vs Gemini, it's **ungraded vs graded.** Chatbots are phenomenal *analysis* tools and catastrophic *signal* tools, and most of this sub's pain comes from mixing those up.

Where LLMs genuinely earn their keep in trading:

* **Research compression** — earnings calls, filings, macro synthesis in minutes instead of hours
* **Building the machine** — writing your backtest code, debugging your pipeline, stress-testing your strategy logic. Claude especially is elite here
* **Red-teaming your thesis** — "argue against this trade" is the highest-EV prompt in finance

Where they silently kill accounts: asking any chatbot *what to trade.* Ask twice, get two answers. There's no track record, no hit rate, no drawdown history — just confident text with zero accountability. An ungraded opinion generator with infinite conviction is the most dangerous instrument ever handed to retail.

The upgrade path is always the same: **use the AI to build something that gets graded, then trust the grade, not the chat.** Backtest out-of-sample, freeze it, forward-track it, and let the record overrule your feelings.

My lane for this is sports markets rather than equities — I run [modelplay.ai](https://modelplay.ai/), where people build and backtest sports betting models with no code, every model gets a frozen out-of-sample backtest, and live picks are tracked publicly against closing lines (the betting version of marking against mid). Sports is honestly a brutal little laboratory for this discipline: daily settlement, a hard benchmark (the close), and nowhere for an ungraded opinion to hide. The lesson transfers 1:1 to trading — the tool that "sounds smartest" and the tool that's *right* are only distinguishable by a frozen record.

So: any frontier LLM for analysis, none of them for signals, and whatever stack forces you to grade yourself. The best AI tool for trading is the one that's allowed to be wrong in public 📊

comments.author: ryank001
comments.body:
honest take — none of them will hand you a good *idea*. ask any of them "what should I buy" and you just get a confident average of the internet, usually half-hallucinated.

where they actually earn their keep is the boring stuff: writing backtest code so you can test an idea instead of trusting a vibe, summarizing earnings/filings fast (but double-check the numbers, they misquote), and poking holes in your own logic — "what's the overfitting/survivorship risk here" is a great use.

i mostly use Claude and ChatGPT, but honestly the tool matters way less than what you point it at. use it to build and stress-test your process, not to pick the trades. the second you're leaning on it for the actual buy/sell call, you've handed away the one part that was supposed to be your edge.

comments.author: Am4nnnn

For sure, totally understand your concern. We strongly believe that people will understand the proof of concept after they’ve tried it themselves. Once things go live, everyone will be able to see how their backtest reflects live. 

Would love for you to try it and give us your honest opinion. As for security/privacy we allow people to opt in to use their data but we don’t use data without their approval. In other words everything is stored safely. 

Also to answer your last concern, our platform uses neuro symbolism in order to get over the LLM-to-code challenge. So everything you are saying is being compiled in real time at an architectural level, no just a pulling data
